# Document Access Clause

Registers existing Timeline Access documents as embedded permission evidence for a document’s Activation checks. Registration records access evidence locally; permission changes remain controlled by the timeline provider.

## Bindings and actions

- `bindings.grants` is a non-root JSON pointer, defaulting to `/documentAccess`. It selects the collection where newly registered access documents are referenced and embedded. Changing it changes that collection’s location, not the provider’s permissions. No initial empty collection is declared.
- `bindings.refresh` is a dictionary of action connections, not a data pointer. Its default connection, `accessRegistered`, runs `refresh` when `/activation/accessPaths` changes. An override replaces this default connection configuration.

`register` has no default connection. Its invocation depends on a configured connection and the applicable authenticated channel. Connection `params` override action defaults; `when` can skip execution, while `parameters.conditions` can reject an action. Connections can also supply `before`, `after` and `once`; `once` defaults to false. These declarations do not establish the current reader’s authority.

## Registration

`register` takes `documents`, defaulting to `trigger.documents`, or `[]` when absent. It requires one to sixteen initialized Timeline Access documents. The storage `basePath` is supplied from `bindings.grants`.

The call must require the exact reviewed document version, and `call/channel` must name an existing party in `/activation/parties`. Otherwise it fails with `ACCESS_EXACT_REVIEW_REQUIRED` or `ONLY_PARTY_LEAD_CAN_MANAGE`. Merely being a listed representative does not satisfy this party-lead check.

Each supplied document must have the Timeline Access type, a `Public Timeline Channel` at `contracts.provider`, an original document at `contracts.initialized.document`, and provider history at `contracts.checkpoint/entries/provider`. Both its original and current executable policies must match the standard provider channel and `update` operation; only the current `initialized` and `checkpoint` contracts are excluded from that comparison. Missing evidence or altered policy rejects registration.

Documents are deduplicated by the identity of their original initialized document. Each new identity receives a reference to the supplied access state under `grants`, and its path is appended to `/activation/accessPaths`. The action also installs an embedded channel for `Timeline Access Updated`, a handler copied from `/contracts/activationInitializedRefresh/steps`, and a registration in `/activation/registeredAccessChannels`.

If every identity is already registered, the result is `duplicate`; existing references are not replaced, even when a later state is supplied. Otherwise the result is `acceptedNew`. Under `outcome-v1`, only `acceptedNew` reaches configured `after` steps or marks a `once` connection as fired. A registration attempt or accepted local registration does not itself create provider permissions.

## Access and activation

Within each confirmed Timeline Access document, every `allowedKeys` key may read every `allowedTimelines` timeline. Either list may be empty. The provider controls atomic replacement of both lists. Read grants do not confer publishing, resharing or business-operation authority. Current permission evidence comes from authenticated provider publication and executed public history; an update notification alone is insufficient.

`refresh` initializes missing terms state and recalculates Activation and pending admission access readiness. For each `Timeline Channel` transport, the local access check requires one access document matching its exact timeline and provider and containing at least one key from every reader group. Groups include configured readers, parties and representatives; an empty group cannot satisfy the check. Partial coverage across separate documents is not combined by this local check, although provider read authorization can be the union of multiple confirmed grants. Transports matching `External Channel` bypass this check. Pending party additions participate when their `expectedRevision` matches the current Activation revision.

The refresh records `accessReady` and `functional` from access coverage. `termsAccepted` requires all required approvals and unchanged agreed fields; `active` additionally requires access and an unclosed document. `status` is `CLOSED` when closed; otherwise it is `WAITING_FOR_ACCESS` before first activation, `SUSPENDED_ACCESS` after previous activation when access is missing, `AWAITING_ACCEPTANCE` when access is available but acceptance is incomplete, or `ACTIVE`. `everActivated` preserves whether activation has ever occurred, rather than indicating current readiness.

A first activation emits `Document Activated`; renewed activation after unavailable access emits `Document Access Restored`; losing access while active emits `Document Access Suspended`. Refresh can also install initial party channels when access becomes ready. These are document lifecycle outcomes, not new provider grants.
